reuse.why: Reuses isTrackingBudget, getCategoryAverage, getSheetValue, setNMonthAvg and the shared extractTagsFromText tag parser; the new action is built on the shared month-fill helpers rather than a fresh query.

duplication.why: The three copied hidden-category queries and the repeated sign flips are replaced by month-fill.ts; what remains repeated is the per-loop `isMonthFillCategory(cat, isTracking)` guard in every action and the hidden/note/goal join written both in getMonthFillCategories and in the extended getBudgetData.

placement.why: A new budget/month-fill.ts module next to actions.ts holds the selection rules, and the new method is registered in budget/app.ts with the same mutator(undoable()) wrapping as its siblings.

scope.why: Changes are confined to the month-wide actions, the shared module, the method registration, tests and a release note.

maintainability.why: Each exclusion rule (hidden with opt-in, #fixed group tag, saved template) lives in one predicate and the sign rule in one function; the income rule is still applied by each caller rather than by the selection function, and toAverageFillAmount is reused for last-month spending under an averaging name.

bypasses_abstraction.where: copyPreviousMonth reads budget rows via getBudgetData but still applies the shared isLockedForMonthFill / isMonthFillCategory predicates; all other month-wide actions use getMonthFillCategories.

disguised_duplication.where: The join of categories, groups and group notes appears in getMonthFillCategories and getBudgetData openly, feeding the same shared predicate; it is not reshaped to hide duplication.

abstraction_drift.where: isLockedForMonthFill / getMonthFillCategories gain the requested includeHiddenCategories option (step 4); the #fixed and template rules are added as general conditions of the predicate, and every month-wide action, including the new setLastMonthSpending and copyPreviousMonth, goes through the shared predicates.
